claimLedger.wording: AmpleCapacity offers a Mac storage scan that explains caches, installers and rebuildable leftovers.
claimLedger.excerpt: AmpleCapacity finds the caches, installers, and leftovers your tools can recreate — then explains what they are before you make a change.
claimLedger.conditions: Product description, not a hands-on result

claimLedger.wording: Scanning and inspecting results are free, with no account or card; a licence is required to move items to the vault.
claimLedger.excerpt: Scanning and inspecting are free and stay free. They only read your disk. A licence is needed to move anything to the vault.
claimLedger.conditions: No purchase or activation tested; download page adds no account or card

claimLedger.wording: Developer is advertised at US$49.99 once for three Macs you own, including build/package caches, container disks and model weights plus Everyday coverage.
claimLedger.excerpt: Developer $49.99 once For people who write code, run containers or keep models on their Mac. Three Macs you own Build and package caches Container disks and model weights Everything in Everyday
claimLedger.conditions: US dollars; tax added at checkout; no subscription; checkout and key enforcement untested

claimLedger.wording: Everyday is advertised at US$24.99 once for five devices in one household, covering iCloud photos/videos, old downloads/installers, iPhone backups, app caches and Trash.
claimLedger.excerpt: Everyday $24.99 once For photos, documents, downloads and everyday use. Five devices in your household Photos and videos already in iCloud Old downloads and installers iPhone backups, app caches and trash
claimLedger.conditions: US dollars; tax added at checkout; devices wording does not establish an iOS or Windows app

claimLedger.wording: The site advertises 20% off both plans with OCTOBER20 until 31 October.
claimLedger.excerpt: 20% off both plans with code OCTOBER20 at checkout, until 31 October.
claimLedger.conditions: Observed October 21, 2026; page does not specify expiry year/timezone; omit from evergreen copy unless rechecked; no discounted checkout total claimed

claimLedger.wording: The terms describe a recovery vault on the same disk, seven-day restoration or thirty days for a Guardian-rule move; permanent emptying ends recovery.
claimLedger.excerpt: AmpleCapacity moves files to a recovery vault on the same disk. It does not delete them at that moment. You can put them back for seven days, or thirty if a Guardian rule made the move. After that window the vault clears itself and the space is returned. Emptying the vault yourself is permanent.
claimLedger.conditions: Not a tested recovery guarantee or backup. Guardian setup, availability and execution conditions not established

claimLedger.wording: The terms say users approve moves, should keep backups and should treat displayed sizes as estimates because APFS shared blocks can inflate them.
claimLedger.excerpt: You decide what to move. The app explains what each item is and what happens if it goes, but you approve every move. Keep your own backups. We are not able to recover anything once the vault has cleared. Sizes on disk are estimates: shared APFS blocks can make them read high.
claimLedger.conditions: Do not turn this into an unconditional per-event approval claim given undocumented Guardian-rule behavior

claimLedger.wording: The download page links a Mac ZIP and says to unzip, drag to Applications, open there and grant disk access when macOS asks.
claimLedger.excerpt: Download for Mac · 6 MB; Unzip, drag it to Applications, open it from there. macOS asks for disk access.
claimLedger.conditions: URL https://amplecapacity.com/downloads/AmpleCapacity.zip; no binary downloaded; 6 MB is advertised, not measured; permission type not specified

claimLedger.wording: The download page advertises Apple signing and notarisation.
claimLedger.conditions: Attribute to vendor only; no binary signature or notarisation ticket inspected

claimLedger.wording: The privacy policy says scans remain on the Mac and lists update checks, licence validation and roughly weekly licence-status requests.
claimLedger.excerpt: File names, paths, sizes, dates and scan summaries are read on your Mac and stay there. The app makes three network calls, and only three. One to check whether a newer version exists. One to validate a licence key when you enter it. One, about once a week, to ask whether your licence key is still valid.
claimLedger.conditions: Policy says two calls in introduction but three in body; also says activation works offline. Do not assert exact call count, entirely offline operation or audited no-telemetry behavior

claimLedger.wording: The vendor says clearing stops after a fortnight of failed licence checks and weekly checks send a one-way key fingerprint.
claimLedger.excerpt: It sends one thing: a one-way fingerprint of your key. If the app cannot reach us it keeps working. It only stops after a fortnight of failed checks
claimLedger.conditions: Policy statement, not tested enforcement; do not equate one-time purchase with indefinitely offline clearing

claimLedger.wording: The vendor states all sales final, subject to processor discretion and legal cancellation rights.
claimLedger.excerpt: AmpleCapacity does not offer refunds. Their buyer terms say refunds are provided at their sole discretion and on a case-by-case basis. Where the law of your country gives you a right to cancel an online purchase of digital goods, that right stands regardless of what this page says.
claimLedger.conditions: Not legal advice; do not omit processor/statutory exceptions

claimLedger.wording: Exact AmpleCapacity version/build, minimum macOS and supported CPU architectures are not verified.
claimLedger.conditions: Mac target is confirmed; do not infer macOS 13+, Intel or Apple Silicon compatibility from Breathing Room requirements

claimLedger.wording: App/helper grouping, CPU/memory monitoring and recurring storage-growth history are not verified for AmpleCapacity.
claimLedger.excerpt: thirty if a Guardian rule made the move
claimLedger.conditions: Guardian mention does not establish a scheduler or parity with daily care; unknown is not No

workflow.title: A recovery vault is not free space: planning a Mac cleanup before a large download
workflow.primaryIntent: Understand why selected reclaimable files and same-disk vault moves do not immediately create enough free space for a large download
outline: Begin with a decision: if space is urgent, understand vault retention before moving anything; keep backups
Top visual: link official AmpleCapacity results only until permission is cleared; no measured savings interpretation
Separate scan estimate, selected files, vault bytes and available space; cite AmpleCapacity APFS warning
Document seven-day normal / thirty-day Guardian vault windows without inventing Guardian configuration
Check rebuild/download cost and backup status; do not treat model weights, container disks or iCloud items as universally expendable
Later visual: Breathing Room Space current-source example preview with full disclosure
Explain the alternative reviewable workflow and Trash/free-space distinction from capabilities.md, then one disclosed recommendation
Decision aid: need space now, need rollback, or need to investigate recurring growth; no destructive tutorial
workflow.interactionPass: Hand off a static decision checklist: required free space, current available space, rebuild cost, backup status, vault-retention deadline. No fake calculator outputs, no filesystem access and no advice to empty vault merely to meet a target.
workflow.distinctness: Mechanism/deadline workflow, not another broad cache-cleaner roundup or expanded pricing matrix
